newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols rise as bonds gyrate.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols rise as bonds gyrate.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. T-bond options edged up, despite the weekend time-decay and an overall positive bias in bond prices, as the market nervously gyrated amid worries over the dollar's freefall, dealers said.
"It's been pretty wild," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.

Most of the biggest option deals were in soon-to-expire June contracts as many traders expected the market to stay choppy next week ahead of the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, he noted.
An investment bank was seen selling June 2,500 contracts of 109 puts early in the session, while another firm bought 2,500 lots of June 109-110 put spread.

June options expire next Friday. Rollovers into July serial options were expected to pick up early next week as July contracts, currently trading in the FLEX options pit, move to the bond pit from Sunday's night session.

Implied volatility for September options rose about half a point to 8.7 percent. June volatility, which was becoming irrelevant as it flip-flopped widely on small changes in premiums or futures prices, stood at around 8.5 percent.
Overall, volatilities were still more sensitive to the bonds' downside risk, traders said.

While the underlying trend in the bond market was looking positive after an early breakout today above last Friday's 110-10/32 high in June futures, the dollar's four-yen drop to about 119 yen fueled concerns that Japanese investors might sell off U.S. assets, they said.
June futures rallied to 110-14/32 in early trade on what was perceived as a softer stance in Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments overnight.
But the market then dived into negative territory as the dollar dropped, only to bounce back up again after finding support well above Thursday's lows.

Eurodollar volatilities were more subdued as the shorter end of the yield curve benefited from growing perception after Greenspan's remarks that the Fed might not raise interest rates at the May FOMC meeting as had been widely anticipated, a trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said.
Implied volatilities for September and December Eurodollar futures options were little changed at around 10.0 and 11.5 percent.
